title: Build real games | Code Like It's 198x
excerpt: Learn programming by building complete games on classic 8-bit and 16-bit systems, in the languages people used at the time.
content_html:
You can make these.

Build real games. Learn what makes them work.
Explore different ideas, genres and ways to program across machines and languages.

Different games.
Different possibilities.

Dodge meteors, crack a code, guide sheep home or time a jump. Each game explores different ideas and the character of its machine.

Never programmed before?

Start with The Basics: give instructions, remember a value and ask for input. No machine or language to choose yet.

Start with The Basics

Different Machines.
Different Ways In.

Choose the machine or language that interests you. The Spectrum is one starting point; the C64, Amiga and NES have their own routes.

Explore the full systems directory

Build Things.
Understand More.

Lessons guide the work. Shared subjects help you open the ideas behind it, and follow them beyond one game, language or machine. Start with the question you have.

The same bits. Two ways to read them.

Binary
00001010

Decimal
10

Representation is an idea you can take to every system.

Maths for Games

Explore chance, direction and movement through experiments you can change. Build a dice experiment, compare sample sizes, or turn coordinates into an aimed shot.

Explore chance and aiming

The Craft

Make deliberate choices about how a game plays. Explore controls, movement and feedback, then test what changing one rule does to the experience.

Try the Game Feel playground

Shared subjects are useful places to enter or return to. They are not a compulsory course to finish before making a game.

Same Curiosity.
Different Possibilities.

See how the lessons use each machine’s character. These are captures from the current courses, rather than a promise that every route has the same coverage.

Safe Cracker

Commodore 64 · BASIC

Can you crack the code? Make a guess, read the clues and narrow the search.

Learn variables, decisions and repetition.

Explore Safe Cracker

Dash

NES · 6502 assembly

Can you time the jump? Read the controller, avoid the hazard and gather coins.

Learn controller input, movement and collisions.

Explore Dash

Flock

Commodore Amiga · 68000 assembly

Can you get the flock home? Dodge the traffic, cross the stream and fill the fold.

Learn hardware sprites, collisions and game states.

Explore Flock

One Game.
One Small First Step.

Meteor Storm’s first lesson moves pixels across a byte boundary. A bit that leaves one byte must arrive in the next. That small idea is the beginning of the ship’s movement.

Start Meteor Storm

What Will
You Make?

New to programming? Begin with The Basics. Have a machine in mind? Choose its route and find something you want to make.
